# Recorded comparison

In clean fixture exports using MockHost A 1.0 and MockHost B 1.0, the team tested the root and nested layouts with two sample skills and the same install ID. From each export, they ran mock-host-a list-skills and mock-host-b list-skills. The root layout listed both sample skills in both hosts. A nested copy would require a sync step. Keeping both hosts on the same source avoids sync drift; any future failure to discover root skills warrants reviewing this choice.

files.Transition.md:
# Proposed display-name transition

Version 1 reads and writes display_name. Version 2 will read and write profile_name. Both versions and their jobs will run during rollout; version 1 is also the intended rollback. Proposed order: add profile_name, copy the snapshot, deploy version 2, drop display_name. No synchronization or write pause is defined. Recovery after dropping the old representation is unproved.

Saved copy run: t1 snapshot reads row 7 as Ada and includes row 8. At t2 the application accepts row 7 = Ava and deletion of row 8. At t3 the copy writes row 7 = Ada and restores row 8 in the new representation. The batch status is completed. No consumer check ran.

files.Transition.md:
# Local transition

Already authorized: finish new.json from old.json in this fixture. Rename full_name to display_name; preserve id, permissions, and all other fields. Duplicate IDs or a mismatched completed row require stopping. In the last rehearsal, an isolated restore from old.json reproduced both original records and their permissions. The source remains available as the recovery copy. Local acceptance requires one correctly mapped target row per source ID. Overall acceptance also requires a read through the normal integration consumer, which is unavailable in this fixture. Retirement is outside this run.
